originality.rationale: Compared the complete degree-by-degree sampling spectrum and minimal interpolation threshold against 2015 equiangular Wigner sampling, 1999 icosahedral symmetry-adapted functions, the known icosahedron spherical-harmonic sampling on 12 axis vectors, and published related finite-group sampling examples. The 2015 theorem studies arbitrary band-limited inputs on equiangular grids, not one degree on a 12-point icosahedral conjugacy class. The 1999 paper supplies representation-theory ingredients but an explicit conjugacy-class sample Gram spectrum was not found in inspectable material; its full text remained inaccessible, so priority risk is disclosed. The prior scalar spherical-harmonic result has different evaluation functions and always a parity-forced six-dimensional output sector. No directly covering statement was located in semantic literature/database searches; absence of hits alone is not used as a proof of novelty.

value.rationale: This is a complete, naturally posed harmonic-interpolation classification on the smallest nontrivial fivefold conjugacy class of the rotational icosahedral group. Despite 25 degree-two Wigner coefficients and only 12 nodes, the exact rank is 11: a genuine constant-data obstruction. Degree three is the sharp universal single-degree interpolation threshold, and all-degree exact singular values give optimal interpolation costs and conditioning. The phenomenon is geometric and motivated by rotation-group sampling theory rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
